trial_court: Family Court, Title Matrimonial Suit No. 300 of 2014
case_name: Janardan Prasad Tiwari vs Arti Devi
facts_of_case: The petitioner filed an application under section 10 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking judicial separation from his wife on the ground of her unsoundness of mind.

legal_principles.principle: Two witnesses should have been accepted by the Court.
legal_principles.held: there is no requirement in law to produce documentary evidence so as to prove mental disorder or unsoundness of mind of a person.

legal_principles.principle: The Court may dissolve a marriage on the ground that the other party has been incurably of unsound mind, or has been suffering continuously or intermittently from mental disorder.
legal_principles.held: Any marriage may be dissolved by a decree of divorce on the ground that other party has been incurably of unsound mind, or, has been suffering continuously or intermittently from mental disorder of such a kind and to such an extent that the petitioner cannot reasonably be expected to live with the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: Mental disorder or unsoundness of mind can be proved through two witnesses.

outcome.final_order: The court set aside the judgment passed by the trial court and allowed the appeal.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for judicial separation
